Hi Ben / Marissa,

We're ramping toward a public launch in Q4 and are trying to lock in commit economics for hosted API usage. Two quick asks: 1) how do you handle temporary launch surge above committed monthly volumes (do you offer crediting or grace buffers?), and 2) can we build step-up monthly commits to reflect a 3-month ramp (25% -> 50% -> 100%) without losing the higher discount tiers?

High level: our traffic profile will be very spiky during the first 8 weeks (multi-region), then smooth out. Procurement copied on this thread — they'll want specifics for contract language and an initial SOW.

Thanks,

Hi Samira — thanks for the context, and congrats on the upcoming launch. Short answers up front: we can support planned launch surges without losing eligibility for higher discount tiers, and we commonly structure a temporary rolling "surge allowance" plus a month-by-month step-up commit schedule that preserves tiered pricing as volume grows.

Key proposal (draft):
- Surge allowance: baseline commit + a temporary buffer equal to 30% of month N commit for up to 6 continuous weeks. Overages beyond the buffer billed at public rate but credited back as a one-time launch credit if monthly commit is increased retroactively.
- Step-up commits: 3-month ramp (Month1=25%, Month2=50%, Month3=100% of target commit). Discounts ladder based on achieved monthly usage against committed thresholds — if LaunchPad hits the target for Month3, the higher discount tier applies retroactively to months where the step-up commit was covered by the buffer/credits.
- True-up: quarterly true-up with a simple reconciliation: if aggregate usage > committed annual volume, apply agreed per-token true-up rate; if <, no clawback (we keep it simple for PLG-friendly onboarding).

I've attached a sample commit schedule and a draft SOW to illustrate billing milestones and where surge credits would be recorded. Please review and flag anything procurement needs to see in contract language.

Attachments: commit_schedule_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), SOW-draft.pdf (pdf)

Samira / Ben / Procurement — jumping in to lock language and make this executable from our side. Below is suggested contract wording + a worked example (feel free to paste into your procurement ticket).

Suggested contract clause (short):
"Launch Surge Allowance: For the first 60 days following a Customer-declared Product Launch, Customer is eligible for a temporary Surge Allowance equal to 30% of the Customer's committed monthly token volume. Usage within the Surge Allowance will not affect the Customer's discount tier eligibility for the committed month. Any usage in excess of the Surge Allowance will be invoiced at the standard overage rate and may be credited retroactively if Customer elects to increase the monthly commit for the affected month within 30 days following the invoice date."

Worked example (3-month ramp to $1.2M/month target):
- Target month (Month 3): 1,200,000 USD equivalent commit -> Discount tier = 25% off public per-token rate (example public = $0.0008/token).
- Month 1 commit = 300,000 USD (25% of target). Surge allowance for Month 1 = 90,000 USD (30% of commit).
- If observed usage Month 1 = 420,000 USD, overage = 30,000 USD billed at public rate, but if Customer upgrades Month 2 commit to 600,000 USD and confirms within 30 days, we will apply a one-time launch credit for the 30,000 USD overage back to the Month 2 invoice.

Operational notes:
- Surge allowances are applied per-account (not per-region) unless regional isolation is contractually required; we can offer per-region buffers as an add-on.
- For audits and invoices we track surge consumption as a separate line item.
- Finance will treat credits as contra-revenue and they will appear on the following invoice cycle where applicable.

Next steps I suggest: Ben to provide the sample per-token math spreadsheet (already attached) and procurement to confirm whether they need per-region isolation in the SOW. If LaunchPad wants per-region, we can provide an alternate SOW that splits the commit into regional buckets.
